proved_step: Proof. Let s_j(i) be the partial sum of gate j over the first i variables. Let P_j(i) = sum_{l>i} max(W_jl,0) and N_j(i) = sum_{l>i} min(W_jl,0), so the final sum lies in [s_j+N_j, s_j+P_j]. Define the class kappa_j(s) = 0 if s+P_j(i) < t_j; 1 if s+N_j(i) >= t_j; and the exact value s otherwise. (1) Exactness: for class 0 or 1 the bottom bit is the same for every completion of the remaining variables; for an undecided s the class is the exact value. So the bit vector of any completion depends only on the class vector. (2) Transitions are well defined: reading x_{i+1} changes P and N by subtracting max(W,0) and min(W,0) at index i+1. If class 0, then s'+P(i+1) <= s+P(i) < t, so s' stays class 0. Class 1 is symmetric. Undecided values are updated exactly. So the class vector at stage i+1 is a function of the class vector at stage i and x_{i+1}. (3) Counting: the DP c_{i+1}(kappa') = sum over (kappa, x_{i+1}) with transition kappa -> kappa' of c_i(kappa) is exact, and at i = n the classes are bits, so #f^{-1}(1) = sum of c_n over class vectors with top(bits) = 1. (4) State bound: at stage i an undecided value of gate j lies in an interval of length P_j(i) - N_j(i) = sum_{l>i}|W_jl| <= B(n-i), so there are at most B(n-i)+2 classes per gate and at most prod_j (B(n-i)+2) class vectors. Summing over i gives O(k n (Bn+2)^k) operations. Scope: fixed k, bounded integer weights; all other bottom gates are irrelevant to f and drop out. Compared with the plain partial-sum DP (state bound (2Bi+1)^k at stage i), the gain is a constant-factor change in the window, not a change of the exponent. Barrier and transfer check: this is a poly(n) algorithm for constant k and B = poly(n), so it cannot transfer to a 2^n/n^{omega(1)} lower-bound hypothesis; no LOWER_BOUND is claimed. Known-type status: counting for a constant number of halfspaces over a bounded-weight cube is standard (Dyer / Frieze-style pseudo-polynomial DP); I have not checked the literature, so novelty is unverified.

proved_step: LEMMA (rank sandwich for OBDD width). Let f:{0,1}^n->{0,1}, let pi be a variable order, and for 1<=l<=n-1 let M_l(f,pi) be the 0/1 matrix with rows indexed by assignments a to the first l variables, columns by assignments b to the remaining variables, entries f(a,b). Let R_l = rank over GF(2) of M_l, and D_l = number of DISTINCT rows of M_l (= number of distinct subfunctions f|_a). Then R_l <= D_l <= 2^{R_l}. Consequently minRank(f) <= min_pi max_l D_l(f,pi) <= 2^{minRank(f)}, where minRank(f) = min_pi max_l R_l(f,pi). PROOF. Let V be the GF(2) row space of M_l, dim V = R_l, so |V| = 2^{R_l}. Every row lies in V, and the rows span V by definition, so the set of distinct rows is a spanning set of V; hence D_l >= R_l. Also the distinct rows are elements of V, so D_l <= |V| = 2^{R_l}. For the consequence: for each pi, max_l R_l <= max_l D_l, so minRank <= min_pi max_l D_l. For pi* attaining minRank, max_l D_l(f,pi*) <= 2^{max_l R_l(f,pi*)} = 2^{minRank}, so min_pi max_l D_l <= 2^{minRank}. Each step is elementary linear algebra over GF(2); no computation is used. SCOPE: all Boolean f, all n>=2, all orders. STATUS OF THE GAP: this sandwich is two-sided but does not decide G0001. The lower side is trivial (D >= R). The upper side gives only the exponential relation, not the reverse direction that G0001 asks for. It is not a P vs NP claim and carries no barrier content (no lower bound is proved).

lemma: S-54f648a904 (formal). Let F = C_1 AND ... AND C_m be a CNF on variables 0..n-1, each clause a set of literals. For S subset of {1..m} let V(S) be the set of variables occurring in clauses of S, and say S is consistent if the assignments that falsify every literal of every clause in S exist, i.e. no variable is required both 0 and 1. Then #F = sum_{S} (-1)^|S| N(S), with N(S) = 2^(n - |V(S)|) if S is consistent and N(S) = 0 otherwise.
proved_step: Proof: an assignment x falsifies C_i for all i in S iff, for each literal l in C_i, x makes l false; so the set of such x is {x : x agrees with the forced values of S}. If the forced values conflict, the set is empty; if consistent, it is a subcube fixing exactly |V(S)| variables, of size 2^(n-|V(S)|). Inclusion-exclusion over the falsified-clause events A_i = {x falsifies C_i} gives #(no A_i) = sum_S (-1)^|S| |intersection_{i in S} A_i|, which is the formula. For t<=p the term is a_t [|b|=t-s]; for t>p it is [|b|=t-s] b_{t-p}. So row a equals F_s(b) + sum_{t=1}^p a_t H_{t-s}(b), with s=|a|, H_u(b)=[|b|=u], F_s(b)=sum_{t=p+1}^n [|b|=t-s] b_{t-p}. Each row lies in V_s = span{F_s, H_{t-s}: 1<=t<=p}, dim <= p+1, and V_s depends only on s in {0..p}. So the row space lies in sum_{s=0}^p V_s, of dimension <= (p+1)^2. Consequence (conditional on H below): the natural order gives W_rank(HWB_n) <= (n+1)^2, so min over orders is <= (n+1)^2. statement: Let F: {0,1}^n -> {0,1} and let S be a set of variables. Let M_S be the cut matrix with rows indexed by assignments to S, columns by assignments to the complement, and entries F. Let K(S) be the number of distinct rows of M_S and R(S) the rank over Q of M_S. Then K(S) <= 2^R(S). Consequently W(F) <= 2^R(F), where W(F) is the min over variable orders of the max over prefixes of K, and R(F) is the min over orders of the max over prefixes of R.
proof: Let r = R(S) and let V be the row space of M_S over Q, so dim V = r. Choose r linearly independent columns J of M_S. Since these columns span the column space, the submatrix M_S[:,J] has rank r, so its row space has dimension r. statement: Let F be a conjunction of m positive EXACT1 clauses, each on three distinct Boolean variables, and fix a variable order whose every prefix cut has at most B crossing clauses. Then #SAT(F) is computable by a dynamic program using at most 2^B states per level and O((m+n(B+1))2^B) arithmetic operations, excluding integer bit complexity and representation overhead.
proof: At each prefix cut, store the partial sum of assigned variables for each crossing clause. Reject any prefix with a partial sum at least 2. For each remaining state, branch on the next variable's two values, update only clauses incident to that variable, and when a clause's last variable is assigned retain the branch exactly when its total sum is 1. Clauses wholly in the unprocessed suffix are untouched. Hence the vector of active sums, each in {0,1}, determines all constraints involving processed variables that can affect a completion. Prefixes with the same vector have the same valid suffix completions, so their counts may be added. There are at most 2^B vectors per level. Each clause-variable incidence is updated once per state at its variable's level; summing degrees gives O(m 2^B) incidence work. Explicit state-vector updates cost O(B) per state per level, hence O(n B 2^B); initialization and finalization add O((m+n)2^B). The total is O((m+n(B+1))2^B). At the final level all clauses have been checked, so the accumulated count is exactly #SAT(F).

statement: For any Boolean function f:X×Y→{0,1}, any fixed cut X|Y, and any field K, let M be its 0/1 communication matrix over K, let r=rank_K(M), and let D be the number of distinct rows of M. Then D≤2^r. Consequently, for every variable order π, the maximum number of residual functions at a cut is at most 2^{max_cut rank_K(M_cut)}; minimizing over π gives W_OBDD(f)≤2^{W_rank,K(f)}.
proof: Let U be the row space of M, of dimension r. The coordinate functionals on K^Y restrict to a spanning set of U*, so choose coordinates y_1,...,y_r whose restrictions form a basis of U*. The map φ:U→K^r given by these coordinates is injective. Every row of M is in U and has only 0/1 entries, so its image lies in {0,1}^r. Distinct rows therefore have distinct images, proving D≤2^r. If r=0, U={0} and D≤1. At a variable-order cut, rows correspond exactly to residual functions on the unprocessed variables. Apply the bound at each cut, then minimize over orders; monotonicity of 2^x gives the stated inequality.

proved_step: statement_start: REPAIR of S0104: Let F be a positive EXACT1 3-CNF on n variables and m clauses with three distinct variables per clause. For a fixed variable order whose every prefix cut has at most B crossing clauses, exact #SAT is computable in O((n+m) * 3^B * poly(B)) arithmetic operations. Proof: Maintain a map from residual signatures to counts. A signature comprises (1) a failure flag, and (2) for each of the at most B crossing clauses, a residual condition from the set {EXACT1 on 3 vars, EXACT1 on 2 vars (sum=1), EXACT1 on 1 var (value=1), forced-0, forced-1, false}. There are at most 7^B * 2 signatures. Initialize with the empty assignment (flag=false, all clauses in future set) with count 1. At step k (variable v = order[k]), for each signature, branch on v=0 and v=1. To update: only clauses containing v change status. For each such clause, update its residual condition in O(1) time using a precomputed transition table (7 states x 2 values). Clauses not containing v keep their condition. After updating both children, merge identical signatures by summing counts. Merging uses hashing: O(7^B * poly(B)) per level. Total work per level: O(3^B * deg(v) * poly(B) + 7^B * poly(B)) = O(3^B * deg(v) * poly(B)) since 7^B = O(3^B * poly(B))? Wait, 7^B is larger than 3^B. Actually max signatures is 2 * 7^B. But the number of *active* signatures is at most 2 * 3^B + 1 because each crossing EXACT1 clause has at most 3 residual conditions when the failure flag is false (sum=0, sum=1, or false), plus the all-false state. So active signatures <= 2 * 3^B + 1. Updating a signature takes O(deg(v)) time (only clauses containing v change). Merging takes O(3^B * poly(B)) via hashing. Sum over n levels: O(3^B * poly(B) * sum_v deg(v) + n * 3^B * poly(B)) = O(3^B * poly(B) * (3m + n)) = O((n+m) * 3^B * poly(B)). At level n, sum counts of signatures with flag=false and no crossing clauses (all satisfied). This proves the runtime bound.

statement_start: REPAIR of S0094: For the positive 1-in-3 formula F(x0,x1,x2) defined by x0+x1+x2=1 with Boolean variables, every variable order has maximum number of distinct residual rows 3 and maximum rational cut-matrix rank 2. Proof: By symmetry it suffices to inspect the order x0,x1,x2 and prefix sizes k=0,1,2,3. At k=0 the single cut row is the full truth table (nonzero), so width=1, rank=1. At k=1, rows indexed by x0=0 and x0=1 over (x1,x2) in order 00,01,10,11: F(0,x1,x2)=EXACT1(x1,x2) gives (0,1,1,0); F(1,x1,x2)=EXACT1(1,x1,x2) gives (1,0,0,0) since 1+x1+x2=1 requires x1=x2=0. These two rows are distinct and linearly independent (a(0,1,1,0)+b(1,0,0,0)=(b,a,a,0)=0 => a=b=0), so width=2, rank=2. At k=2, rows for (x0,x1)=00,01,10,11: 00->F(0,0,x2)=x2 gives (0,1); 01->F(0,1,x2)=1-x2 gives (1,0); 10->same as 01 gives (1,0); 11->impossible gives (0,0). Three distinct rows: (0,1),(1,0),(0,0), spanning 2D space, so width=3, rank=2. At k=3, rows are the values of F, both 0 and 1 occur, width=2, rank=1. Thus maxima over all cuts are 3 distinct rows and rank 2.

evidence: The proof correctly bounds the rational rank by D = prod_{e in C} d_e. For each assignment z to the cut edges, the A-side contraction yields u_z(x_A) and the B-side yields v_z(x_B). The sum over z of u_z(x_A)v_z(x_B) expresses M as a sum of D rank-1 matrices (outer products). Over any field (here Q), the rank of a sum of D rank-1 matrices is at most D. Cancellation can only reduce the rank, never increase it. The argument holds for arbitrary rational tensors, arbitrary signs, and finite external input domains. No counterexample exists; the bound is tight in general (e.g., a tensor network implementing a matrix multiplication of dimensions matching the cut).

The frontier signature can be represented by a failure flag and, for each crossing clause, its residual requirement (one or zero remaining true variables); expired clauses are checked when their last variable is assigned. For a fixed cut there are at most 3^B nonfailed signatures, since each crossing clause has at most these two residual requirements and clauses with no remaining variables are removed after checking. Branching on a variable updates only incident clauses; summing the per-level incidence work gives O((n+m)3^B poly(B)). Thus the stated correctness and bound follow, with the active-signature argument made explicit.

Then min_pi W_rank(pi) <= min_pi W_OBDD(pi) <= 2^(min_pi W_rank(pi)). Proof: At a cut whose matrix has rank r, choose r pivot coordinates such that projection of its row space to those coordinates is injective. Every residual row is binary, so its projection is in {0,1}^r; hence there are at most 2^r distinct residual rows. Therefore W_OBDD(pi) <= 2^W_rank(pi) for each order pi. Since there are finitely many orders, choose pi* minimizing W_rank. Then min_pi W_OBDD(pi) <= W_OBDD(pi*) <= 2^W_rank(pi*) = 2^(min_pi W_rank(pi)). The lower bound follows since rank is at most the number of distinct rows at every cut, hence W_rank(pi) <= W_OBDD(pi) for each pi.

statement: Finite-alphabet row bound. Let F be a field, A a finite subset of F, and M an arbitrary matrix over F whose entries all lie in A. If rank_F(M)=r and D is the number of distinct rows of M, then D<=|A|^r. Proof: Choose a basis b_1,...,b_r of the row space. There are r coordinate positions j_1,...,j_r such that the r-by-r matrix (b_i[j_t]) is nonsingular: this follows because the coordinate functionals restricted to the r-dimensional row space span its dual, so a basis can be selected from them. Consequently the restriction map from the row space to these r coordinates is injective. Distinct rows therefore have distinct restrictions to j_1,...,j_r. Each restriction belongs to A^r, which has |A|^r elements, proving the bound. For a Boolean cut matrix, A={0,1}, so every cut with field rank r has at most 2^r distinct residual rows. For any fixed variable order pi, taking maxima over cuts gives W_OBDD(pi)<=2^W_rank(pi). Taking an order minimizing W_rank yields min_pi W_OBDD(pi)<=2^(min_pi W_rank(pi)); and rank<=number of distinct rows at each cut gives the reverse inequality min_pi W_rank(pi)<=min_pi W_OBDD(pi). This supplies the pivot-coordinate proof for the minimum-over-orders comparison, without relying on S0126.
proof: The coordinate functionals on an r-dimensional subspace of F^N span its dual: if their span were proper, a nonzero vector of the subspace would be annihilated by every coordinate functional, hence would be the zero vector, contradiction. Select r coordinate functionals forming a dual basis. Their joint restriction is injective. Distinct matrix rows are distinct vectors in the row space, so injectivity gives distinct coordinate tuples. Since every entry is in A, there are at most |A|^r such tuples. The Boolean cut-matrix corollary follows with A={0,1}. For the order comparison, the per-cut bounds imply W_OBDD(pi)<=2^W_rank(pi) for every pi. A rank-minimizing order exists because there are finitely many variable orders; using it gives the upper bound on the minimum. At each cut rank is at most the number of distinct rows, giving the lower bound pointwise and thus after minimization.

For every integer k≥1, let F_k be the Boolean function on 3k variables that accepts exactly assignments having Hamming weight one on each of k disjoint triples. In the variable order that processes each triple consecutively, every cut has at most three distinct residual rows and rational cut-matrix rank at most two, and both maxima are attained. Proof: At a cut between triples, any prefix violating a completed constraint gives the zero residual; every other prefix gives the same nonzero suffix function. Thus there are at most two rows and rank at most one. At a cut inside a triple, completed triples again yield either zero or a common factor 1. If t∈{1,2} variables of the current triple have been assigned and their sum is a, its residual is the indicator that the remaining variables sum to 1−a. For a>1 it is zero. For a≤1, the only possible nonzero residuals are the indicators of two different target sums, 1 and 0. The unprocessed triples contribute a common nonzero suffix factor. Therefore there are at most two nonzero rows plus the zero row; the two nonzero rows are linearly independent over Q because their supports are disjoint and nonempty. Hence the rank is at most two. At a cut after two variables of a triple, the three residuals (indicator of the last variable being 1, indicator of it being 0, and zero), each extended by the same nonzero suffix factor, are all attained. Thus both maxima are attained.

statement: Block-product lemma (scoped constructive special case). Let k>=1 and let f_i:{0,1}^{b_i}->{0,1} be nonzero Boolean functions on pairwise disjoint variable blocks. Define F(x^(1),...,x^(k))=product_i f_i(x^(i)), and use an order that processes the blocks consecutively, with any fixed internal order within each block. At any cut lying inside block j, each prefix induces either the zero residual, or a residual of f_j multiplied by the fixed nonzero suffix function product_{i>j} f_i; therefore the number of distinct residual rows is at most D_j+1, where D_j is the maximum number of distinct residual rows of f_j over its internal cuts. The cut matrix rank over any field is at most R_j, the maximum internal cut rank of f_j. At block boundaries the residual count is at most 2 and rank at most 1. Thus W_OBDD(F) <= max(2, 1+max_j D_j), and W_rank(F) <= max(1,max_j R_j), in this block order. Proof: A prefix either falsifies an already completed block (giving the zero row) or satisfies every completed block (whose product is 1); within the current block its continuation is exactly one residual of f_j, and the unprocessed blocks contribute the same nonzero suffix factor to every such row. Distinct nonzero residuals remain distinct after multiplication by a nonzero Boolean function, since that suffix has at least one satisfying assignment. Their span dimension is unchanged by adjoining zero and by tensoring each row with the same nonzero suffix vector, so the rank is at most R_j. At a boundary the only rows are zero and the common suffix product. This is a constructive fixed-order bound for disjoint block products; it does not settle the minimum-over-orders gap G0001.

evidence: The proof is correct: for any field F and any r-dimensional subspace V of F^N (the row space of a cut matrix), the coordinate functionals restricted to V span the dual space V*. If their span were proper, there would exist a nonzero v in V annihilated by all coordinate functionals, implying v=0, contradiction. Thus we can select r coordinate functionals forming a dual basis, giving an injective restriction V -> F^r. Since every residual row is binary, its projection lies in {0,1}^r, yielding at most 2^r distinct rows per cut. Hence W_OBDD(pi) <= 2^W_rank(pi) for each pi. Taking pi* minimizing W_rank gives min_pi W_OBDD(pi) <= 2^(min_pi W_rank(pi)). The lower bound W_rank(pi) <= W_OBDD(pi) holds pointwise because distinct rows are distinct vectors, so rank cannot exceed the number of distinct rows. Minimizing over pi preserves the inequality. No counterexample exists; the argument is general and valid for all fields.

statement: Let M be a matrix over any field whose entries all lie in {0,1}. If rank(M)=r, then M has at most 2^r distinct rows. Proof: let U be the row space of M, of dimension r. Choose r coordinate positions J such that the coordinate projection pi_J: U -> F^r is injective; such positions exist by taking pivot columns of a matrix whose rows are a basis of U. Every row of M lies in U and has entries in {0,1}. If two rows have the same projection, injectivity implies they are the same row. The image of the set of distinct rows is contained in {0,1}^r, a set of cardinality 2^r, proving the bound. statement: Let k>=1, let f_i:{0,1}^{b_i}->{0,1} be nonzero Boolean functions on pairwise disjoint blocks, and let F=product_{i=1}^k f_i. Fix ANY variable order on all variables and any cut. For each i, let A_i|B_i be the split of block i induced by the cut, and let M_i be the matrix with rows indexed by assignments to A_i, columns by assignments to B_i, and entries f_i(a_i,b_i). Then, up to row and column permutations, the cut matrix M_F equals the Kronecker product tensor_i M_i. Consequently rank_F(M_F)=product_i rank_F(M_i) over every field F. Moreover the distinct residual functions of F at this cut are exactly the products tensor_i r_i over tuples of distinct residuals r_i of f_i, and their number is the product of the per-block distinct residual counts. Proof: under the canonical product indexing of assignments to the union of the A_i and B_i, F(a_1,...,a_k,b_1,...,b_k)=product_i f_i(a_i,b_i), which is exactly the entrywise definition of the Kronecker product; changing from concatenated block indices to the chosen global variable order only permutes rows and columns. Rank multiplicativity of Kronecker products over a field gives the rank identity. For residuals, the row indexed by tuple (a_i) is the pointwise product of the residual functions r_i(b_i)=f_i(a_i,b_i). Every tuple is represented. Injectivity follows because each f_i is nonzero, so each residual tuple can be distinguished by fixing all other blocks to satisfying assignments of their f_j; if two tuples differ in block i, choose b_i witnessing differing residual values and satisfying suffix assignments in every other block. Thus distinct tuple count is the product. This exact factorization holds for every cut and every interleaving order; it does not by itself establish an unbounded min-over-orders separation for general Boolean functions.

refuted_approach: S0134's claim that the global distinct residual count equals the product of per-block residual counts is false when zero residuals occur. Tuples with a zero component all give the same global zero residual. Repair: at a fixed cut, let q_i count distinct nonzero residuals of block i, and z_i indicate whether block i has a zero residual. The global count is product_i q_i + 1[sum_i z_i>0]. The nonzero products are distinct because for a differing coordinate j, choose an assignment distinguishing the two nonzero residuals there and satisfying assignments for all other nonzero residuals. The zero residual exists exactly if some z_i=1. The Kronecker rank identity is unaffected.

For tuples of nonzero residuals, the product map is injective: for two different tuples choose coordinate j where r_j differs and an assignment b_j on which they differ; since each other residual is nonzero, choose for each other coordinate an assignment where it equals 1.
